questions.question: Which prompt indicates user EXEC on a device named Edge?
questions.explanation: The greater-than sign marks ordinary user EXEC in this IOS prompt.

option_explanations.C: The greater-than sign marks ordinary user EXEC in this IOS prompt.
option_explanations.D: A plain # indicates privileged EXEC here.

questions.question: Which command changes Edge> to Edge# after successful authentication?
questions.explanation: enable enters privileged EXEC from user EXEC.

option_explanations.A: disable goes from privileged EXEC toward user EXEC.
option_explanations.B: enable enters privileged EXEC from user EXEC.
option_explanations.C: configure terminal requires privileged EXEC and enters global configuration.
option_explanations.D: end exits configuration mode and is not a privilege escalation command.

questions.question: At Edge#, which command opens global configuration mode?
questions.explanation: configure terminal enters the global configuration context from privileged EXEC.

option_explanations.A: configure terminal enters the global configuration context from privileged EXEC.
option_explanations.B: exit leaves the EXEC session from this prompt.
option_explanations.C: Select an interface after entering global configuration mode.
option_explanations.D: At Edge# the session is already in privileged EXEC.

questions.question: At Edge(config)#, which command selects an existing routed port for configuration?
questions.explanation: The interface command enters the selected port's configuration context.

option_explanations.A: The interface command enters the selected port's configuration context.
option_explanations.B: configure terminal is the transition from privileged EXEC, and global configuration is already active.
option_explanations.C: show displays interface information rather than selecting it for editing.
option_explanations.D: do executes an EXEC show command and leaves the configuration context unchanged.

questions.question: At Edge(config-if)#, which command returns to Edge(config)#?
questions.explanation: exit steps back one level from interface configuration.

option_explanations.A: disable lowers EXEC privilege rather than backing out one configuration level.
option_explanations.B: enable enters privileged EXEC from user EXEC.
option_explanations.C: exit steps back one level from interface configuration.
option_explanations.D: end jumps directly to privileged EXEC rather than global configuration.

questions.question: Which command leaves Edge(config-if)# and goes directly to Edge#?
questions.explanation: end returns to privileged EXEC from nested configuration modes.

option_explanations.A: exit backs out only to global configuration mode.
option_explanations.B: end returns to privileged EXEC from nested configuration modes.
option_explanations.C: disable is an EXEC privilege command.
option_explanations.D: do show version displays information without leaving the interface context.

questions.question: Which command displays the active configuration from Edge(config-if)# without leaving that mode?
questions.explanation: do allows an EXEC command to run from a configuration context.

option_explanations.A: A bare show running-config is an EXEC command here.
option_explanations.B: do allows an EXEC command to run from a configuration context.
option_explanations.C: end must be entered separately and leaves configuration mode.
option_explanations.D: configure terminal is a mode transition rather than the requested display.

questions.question: You want a console at Edge# to stay connected with ordinary user EXEC privileges. Which command fits?
questions.explanation: disable lowers the privilege level. exit at the EXEC level can close the session.

option_explanations.A: exit closes the EXEC session instead of keeping it open.
option_explanations.B: disable lowers the privilege level. exit at the EXEC level can close the session.
option_explanations.C: configure terminal enters global configuration mode.
option_explanations.D: end exits configuration mode, and this prompt is already in EXEC.

questions.question: A worksheet says to run hostname Core from interface configuration, then stay in global configuration. Which sequence works?
questions.explanation: exit reaches global configuration, where IOS accepts hostname.

option_explanations.A: exit reaches global configuration, where IOS accepts hostname.
option_explanations.B: disable is not the way out of interface configuration, and hostname requires global configuration.
option_explanations.C: end lands at privileged EXEC, where hostname is not a configuration command.
option_explanations.D: do runs EXEC commands rather than moving a global configuration command into interface mode.

questions.question: Refer to the configuration prompt. Which command changes the current port's description directly from this prompt?
questions.explanation: The config-if prompt provides the context for the description subcommand.

option_explanations.A: interface selects a port from global configuration and is not the syntax for its description.
option_explanations.B: do calls EXEC commands, while description is a configuration command.
option_explanations.C: The config-if prompt provides the context for the description subcommand.
option_explanations.D: hostname sets the device name from global configuration, not the current port description.
